title: Podcast EP360: IDA Ireland’s Role to Expand Ireland’s Footprint Across the Semiconductor Ecosystem with Anne-Marie Tierney - Semiwiki
gist: A 255-word podcast show-note stub (13:38 episode) rather than an article: IDA Ireland's Anne-Marie Tierney frames Ireland as a 50-year European semiconductor hub, naming Analog Devices, AMD, Qualcomm and ASML operations plus a recent $5 billion Intel investment, and describes an incentives/workforce/R&D package to attract more supply-chain investment. The text is a promotional blurb with no numbers beyond the Intel figure, so extraction is deliberately light.

themes.theme: Ireland as European semiconductor investment node

insights.claim: Ireland has a 50-year history as the hub for semiconductor innovation in Europe, per IDA Ireland's semiconductor-focused divisional manager — a positioning claim aimed at competing with continental EU Chips Act destinations for supply-chain investment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ireland is actively marketing itself against Germany/France for European semiconductor capacity — relevant to where the next round of EU fab and supply-chain announcements lands.
insights.quote: Anne-Marie describes Ireland’s 50-year history as the hub for semiconductor innovation in Europe.

insights.claim: Intel recently made a $5 billion investment in Ireland, adding to major existing operations there from Analog Devices, AMD, Qualcomm and ASML.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concrete capex datapoint for Intel's non-US footprint and evidence that Ireland retains leading-edge fab investment despite Intel's capital discipline pressure.
insights.quote: including Analog Devices, AMD, Qualcomm, ASML and a recent $5 billion investment by Intel
insights.locator: She explains that many top semiconductor companies have invested

insights.claim: IDA Ireland's semiconductor pitch bundles workforce development, government incentives, advanced R&D, academic ecosystem development and scaling support rather than leading with tax alone — a multi-lever industrial-policy approach to attracting supply-chain operations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals that talent pipeline and R&D subsidy, not corporate tax rate, are now the competitive levers in EU semiconductor site selection.
insights.locator: She describes the broad focus and commitment

insights.claim: IDA Ireland's stated remit spans the whole global semiconductor supply chain rather than fabs alone, indicating the agency is targeting equipment, materials, design and back-end operations as well as manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Watch for Irish announcements in equipment/materials and design centers, not just wafer capacity, as the likelier form of incremental investment.
insights.locator: who explains how the organization focuses on and promotes investment
